source_text: Περὶ τοῦ τοὺς ἐξαμαρτάνοντας ἐν διαφόροις πταίσματι, καὶ προσκαρτεροῦντας τῇ προσευχῇ τῆς ἐξομολογήσεως καὶ μετανοίας, καὶ τὴν ἀποοτροφὴν τῶν κακῶν τελείαν ποιούμενους, κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τοῦ πταίσματος, καιροῦ μετανοίας δοθέντος τοῖς τοιούτοις, διὰ τοὺς οἰκτιρμοὺς καὶ τὴν ἀγαθότητα τοῦ Θεοῦ προσάγεσθαι τῇ κοινωνίᾳ. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Διορίζει ο παρών Κανών, ότι καν εις διάφορα αμαρτήματα πέση τινας, εξομολογειται δε αυτά και αποστρέφεται και μισει, προσευχόμενος και μετανοων εις τον Θεόν• ο τοιουτος αφ’ ου δοθη εις αυτόν από τον Πνευματικόν καιρός μετανοίας και ικανοποιήσεως, ανάλογος με τά κακά οπου εκαμε, πρέπει να συγχωρηται, και να μεταλαμβάνη τα θεια Μυστήρια, όχι διά την σπουδήν και αξιότητά του, αλλά διά την απειρον φιλανθρωπίαν και τους οικτιρμούς του Θεου, οστις δέχεται πάντας τους είς αυτόν επιστρέφοντας, και ουδεμία αμαρτία είναι η νικωσα την αυτου αγαθότητα, Ορα και τον ιβ΄. της ά.
orientation: The council is decreeing how sinners who repent and persist in prayer are to be brought back to communion.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning those who sin in various faults, and who persist in the prayer of confession and repentance, and who make the turning away from evils complete, according to the proportion of the fault, a time of repentance having been given to such persons, because of the mercies and the goodness of God, they are to be brought to communion. Interpretation. The present Canon determines that even if someone falls into various sins, but confesses them and turns away from them and hates them, praying and repenting to God; such a person, after a time of repentance and satisfaction is given to him by the Spiritual Father, proportional to the evils which he did, must be forgiven, and must partake of the divine Mysteries, not because of his diligence and worthiness, but because of the infinite love for humanity and the mercies of God, who receives all those returning to him, and no sin is one that conquers his goodness. See also the 12th of the first.

choices.english: they are to be brought to communion
choices.why: The passive infinitive with the dative expresses admission to communion as the council's decree; 'brought' preserves the passive force of προσάγεσθαι.
rejected: they should be admitted to communion
let them be received into communion

choices.english: the turning away from evils complete
choices.why: Keeps the adjective τελείαν in its emphatic postposition, preserving the source's word order and the sense of a complete renunciation.

choices.english: a time of repentance having been given
choices.why: The genitive absolute is rendered literally to preserve the temporal conditionality of the source.
rejected: when a time of repentance is given
after a period of repentance has been assigned

choices.term: διὰ τοὺς οἰκτιρμοὺς καὶ τὴν ἀγαθότητα τοῦ Θεοῦ
choices.english: because of the mercies and the goodness of God
choices.why: The causal διὰ is rendered as 'because of' to show that God's mercy, not human merit, is the ground of readmission.
rejected: through the mercies and goodness of God
on account of God's mercies and goodness

choices.why: In the interpretation this is a technical term for the confessor who assigns penance; capitalized to mark the office.
ἄπειρον means boundless or infinite; 'love for humanity' renders φιλανθρωπία as the divine attribute rather than a generic 'kindness'.

pass_b_english: Concerning those who sin in various ways and persist in the prayer of confession and repentance, and who make a complete turning away from evils: after a time of repentance has been given to such persons in proportion to their offense, they are to be brought to communion because of the mercies and the goodness of God.

Interpretation. This present canon decrees that even if someone falls into various sins, but confesses them and turns away from them and hates them, praying and repenting before God—such a person, once a time of repentance and satisfaction has been given to him by the Spiritual Father, proportionate to the evils he has done, must be forgiven and receive the divine Mysteries. This is not because of his own diligence or worthiness, but because of the infinite love for humanity and the mercies of God, who receives all who turn back to him, and no sin overcomes his goodness. See also canon 12 of the first council.
notes: The source text contains a misspelling: ἀποοτροφὴν for ἀποστροφήν in the canon portion; the interpretation has the correct ἀποστρέφεται.
The interpretation is written in a later, simplified Greek with some vernacular features (e.g., 'οπου εκαμε', 'να συγχωρηται').
The final cross-reference 'ιβ΄. της ά.' is abbreviated and refers to canon 12 of the first council, as the context indicates.

last_rejected.quote: persist in the prayer of confession and repentance
last_rejected.source_quote: προσκαρτεροῦντας τῇ προσευχῇ τῆς ἐξομολογήσεως καὶ μετανοίας
last_rejected.why: προσκαρτεροῦντας means persevere/continue, not persist in prayer specifically; the phrase is 'persevering in the prayer of confession and repentance'
last_rejected.fix: persevering in the prayer of confession and repentance
last_rejected.ruling: Persist and persevere are synonyms; 'persist in the prayer' accurately renders προσκαρτεροῦντας τῇ προσευχῇ.

last_rejected.quote: a complete turning away from evils
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν ἀποστροφὴν τῶν κακῶν τελείαν ποιούμενους
last_rejected.why: ποιούμενους is middle voice 'making/doing for themselves', not merely 'make'; 'who make for themselves a complete turning away'
last_rejected.fix: who make for themselves a complete turning away from evils
last_rejected.ruling: Middle ποιούμενους rendered 'make' is within normal range; 'make for themselves' adds nuance but no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: after a time of repentance has been given to such persons in proportion to their offense
last_rejected.source_quote: κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τοῦ πταίσματος, καιροῦ μετανοίας δοθέντος τοῖς τοιούτοις
last_rejected.why: Word order shows 'in proportion to the offense' modifies the time given, but English obscures that the proportion determines the time length
last_rejected.fix: a time of repentance proportionate to their offense having been given to such persons
last_rejected.ruling: English 'after a time...given...in proportion to their offense' preserves the proportional relationship; word order is stylistic.

last_rejected.why: ὁ Πνευματικός is 'the spiritual one/father', but in context this refers to the confessor/priest who assigns penance; capitalized 'Spiritual Father' suggests a technical office
last_rejected.ruling: Πνευματικόν in canonical penitential context means confessor/spiritual father; standard rendering, not misleading.

last_rejected.why: ἱκανοποίησις here means 'satisfaction' in the penitential sense of completing penance, but 'satisfaction' in modern English is misleading; better 'satisfaction' or 'adequate penance'
last_rejected.ruling: ἱκανοποίησις as 'satisfaction' is standard penitential terminology; no meaning changed or reader misled.

last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδεμία ἁμαρτία ἐστὶν ἡ νικῶσα τὴν αὐτοῦ ἀγαθότητα
last_rejected.why: ἡ νικῶσα is 'the one conquering/overcoming', i.e., 'no sin is strong enough to conquer his goodness'; current rendering weakens the active force
last_rejected.fix: no sin is able to conquer his goodness
last_rejected.ruling: 'Overcomes' adequately renders νικῶσα; 'conquering' is a synonym preference, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: τῆς α΄ refers to 'the first [council]', but in context this means Nicaea (325), not just 'the first council' generically; should specify 'First Ecumenical Council' or 'Nicaea'
last_rejected.fix: canon 12 of the First Council of Nicaea
last_rejected.ruling: τῆς α΄ = 'the first [council]'; 'first council' is literal and correct; specifying Nicaea is a preference, not an error.
